transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-09
Start: 15:30 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Eliot (CSM), Priya (Head of ML), Tom (Platform), Lena (Product), Ravi (SRE)

Agenda: quick status, heatmap walkthrough, regression anomalies, guardrail updates, next steps

[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight, quick status from our side then heatmap walkthrough. apologies for the slight audio hiss, should be okay.
[00:28] Priya: yeah thanks samira, we've been running the pilot on staging, saw a spike in false positives last night in the invoice parser flow. wanted to surface that.
[00:45] Diego: quick clarification, when you say false positives do you mean the model returning a confident but incorrect extraction, or wrong intent classification?
[01:03] Priya: confident incorrect extraction — like amounts parsed into the wrong field. scoring shows our precision dropped from 0.92 to 0.78 on that slice.
[01:18] Samira: ok that's what we'll dig into. we pulled the eval heatmap — i'll share the sheet after the call — but quick snapshot: the regression correlates with prompts that include multi-line footers and certain currency symbols.
[01:40] Tom: we pushed a config change to tokenization yesterday too, could be related, but reproductions look model-side.
[01:55] Diego: noted — two tracks: infra / tokenizer vs model prompt fidelity. i'll show the heatmap now.

[02:10] Diego: (screen) heatmap row = prompt bucket, col = metric delta (precision/recall/p95 latency). see this cluster here — bucket 17 — lots of weight on multi-line footers. we also instrumented a score delta flag that marks >0.1 precision drop.
[02:45] Lena: the buckets are new to us — can you explain how you grouped prompts?
[02:55] Diego: yeah, we used your taxonomy Priya sent last week plus clustering on token length and special char frequency. grouping is approximate, we flagged high-impact buckets for manual review.
[03:20] Priya: ok that helps. the golden outputs live in /s3/novaqube/pilot/gold — i'll share access.

[03:40] Samira: another datapoint — in bucket 17 p95 latency stayed stable ~220ms on Redwood Hosted, but p50 increased slightly. so not a latency induced hallucination, more likely prompt ambiguity or training/regression in model weights.
[04:05] Ravi: staging nodes reported a transient OOM but that was earlier during a large-batch run, unrelated i think.
[04:18] Diego: also saw that KV cache hits are lower for these multi-line prompts; maybe prefix matching fails because of newline tokens. we can enable prefix normalization as an experiment.

[04:40] Priya: can Redwood run a controlled experiment: (A) enable prefix normalization + small prompt rewrite, (B) keep baseline? we want to see whether normalization recovers precision.
[04:55] Samira: yes we can. Diego, how long to instrument and run 1k samples?
[05:03] Diego: estimate 24 hours to set up the job and collect results. we'll use Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching and keep quantization constant.

[05:20] Eliot: quick note on scoring: we pushed the weighted F1 > 0.88 as an SLO, but for these legal invoice cases the product team wants 0.95 precision on monetary fields. tradeoff there.
[05:40] Lena: we can tolerate slightly higher latency during the extraction path if accuracy improves, team preference is accuracy over latency for billing-critical flows.
[05:52] Samira: makes sense — we'll treat that bucket as high-priority.

[06:05] Priya: another anomaly — on 2027-03-07 we saw a handful of outputs flagged by guardrails for PII leakage, but the content doesn't contain PII; looks like over-aggressive pattern matching.
[06:24] Diego: are those guardrails running in the request pipeline or post-response?
[06:31] Priya: post-response. we use a regex-based guardrail + lightweight NER.
[06:38] Diego: ok we can tune the guardrail thresholds and add an allowlist for invoice templates. Diego: i'll prepare a suggested regex change and an allowlist config.

[06:50] Samira: also want to call out fallback behavior — we saw the system fallback to a smaller model variant for brief capacity spikes yesterday; precision dropped as expected. we recommend pinning this flow to Dedicated for the pilot if you want tighter fidelity.
[07:10] Tom: cost is a hard constraint; we need an estimate of delta between Hosted and Dedicated for your recommended configuration.
[07:20] Samira: i'll include a cost delta in the follow-up. rough back-of-envelope: Dedicated brings better p95 consistency and fewer fallbacks, might be +25–40% committed cost, but saves manual review time. we'll quantify.

[07:40] Priya: any security questions here? we will need audit logs and SSO soon.
[07:47] Eliot: yes, Redwood can provide audit logs to your SIEM and SAML SSO; we'll send the SOC 2 + ISO docs and a short checklist for VPC peering.
[07:57] Ravi: for VPC we need to test a staging peered flow; i'll open a ticket and grant the minimal role.

[08:10] Diego: back to heatmap — i want to highlight a low-volume bucket with high recall drop; those are edge rejection cases. we propose two mitigations: prompt reheating (explicit instruction templates) and a small reranker that checks numeric field consistency.
[08:35] Priya: reranker is attractive if it's cheap. any perf penalty?
[08:40] Diego: negligible if we keep it as a light scoring pass; adds ~30ms p95 but boosts precision significantly on money fields — we'll simulate.

[09:00] Samira: let's prioritize experiments: 1) prefix normalization + prompt rewrite (Diego), 2) guardrail regex tuning + allowlist (Diego + Priya), 3) reranker sim on 1k sample set (Diego + Priya).

[09:20] Priya: timeline wise we want results before next week's product review, so 3/15 is target.
[09:28] Samira: ok added to next steps.

[09:40] Tom: question about telemetry — can we get per-token cost breakdown on the heatmap? currently we only see aggregate cost.
[09:50] Diego: Redwood Console can break down token cost per-route and per-prompt bucket; i'll include a CSV export with token counts and estimated unit cost.

[10:05] Priya: also, we're worried about regression drift during model rollouts — is there an automated rollback playbook?
[10:15] Eliot: yes, Redwood supports canary rollouts + automatic rollback when evaluation score drops below threshold. we can configure per-route thresholds and an emergency rollback window.

[10:30] Ravi: we'd like a dry-run of rollback so ops understands the path.
[10:35] Samira: we'll schedule a rollback drill. propose Wed 3/16 10:00 PT.

[10:45] Diego: one more technical note — KV cache mismatch could be exacerbated by whitespace tokens, we recommend normalizing whitespace and testing both with and without cache warming. that'll be part of the 1k job.

[11:05] Priya: ok that sounds thorough. I'll assemble the golden outputs and send access by EOD 3/10.

Recap (Samira):
- Redwood will share the eval heatmap CSV, scoring rubric, and cost delta (due 3/11)
- Diego will run prefix-normalization experiment and reranker sim on 1k prompts (results 3/13)
- Customer to send golden outputs + prompt taxonomy (Priya, due 3/15)
- Schedule canary rollback drill 3/16 10:00 PT (all)
- Action items logged in CRM id CRM-78910

[11:40] Lena: thanks everyone, useful call.
[11:45] Samira: thanks all, we'll follow up with links — heatmap, sandbox runner, and a short playbook.
[11:52] Priya: thanks team, talk soon.

Links referenced: https://redwood.com/pilot/heatmap (heatmap CSV), https://s3.aws/novaqube/pilot/gold (golden outputs)

End of transcript.
